question: Can a 27B ternary model be executed under a resident-RAM budget substantially below its packed weight size by treating RAM as a bounded working window and SSD as a backing tier without sacrificing foreground survival?
frozen_hypotheses: Decode is the adversarial phase because a nonresident dense block must be revisited on every generated token unless it remains pinned.
Prefill can amortize block-load cost across many input tokens and should tolerate a smaller resident window than decode.
Increasing resident budget should reduce streamed bytes per decode token monotonically until all blocks are resident.
SSD bandwidth creates a phase boundary but cannot by itself erase the dense decode reread cost.
Pressure-aware shrinking should preserve foreground work before process sacrifice is considered.
stop_conditions_for_physical_followup: foreground task is killed or becomes unresponsive
memory pressure enters an uncontrolled full-stall regime
I/O queueing invalidates the bounded-latency assumption
runtime semantics differ from the modeled layer residency assumptions
nonclaims: No claim that stock llama.cpp currently exposes per-block eviction controls required by the physical design.
No claim that the synthetic 768 MiB runtime/KV reserve represents the user's host.
No claim that SSD streaming will deliver usable interactive decode speed.
No claim that a successful analytic window implies a successful physical run.
No host process is controlled by this PR.
